data.body:
Correction, and it is the one that matters most for judging whether this epic delivered: **the BuildKit cap is NOT holding.** I asserted twice above that it was, and I was wrong in a way that inverted the evidence.

**What I claimed.** In two comments I wrote that "the BuildKit cap IS working — the number is bounded because something bounds it", citing `docker_buildkit_cache_used_percent` pinned at 99-100% as positive evidence. I even used it as the contrast case against the defective `docker_unaccounted_bytes`, on the grounds that a direct ratio against a known budget could not mislead the way a difference of incommensurable units could.

**What is actually true.** Measured on the host via `docker system df`:

    Build Cache   5.875 GB   104 entries   0 active

against `builder.gc.maxUsedSpace` = 5.00 GiB = 5.368 GB. The true ratio is **~109%**. The cache is roughly 0.5 GB PAST its budget, with zero active entries — so this is retained reclaimable cache, not work in progress.

**Why the metric said 100.** `pct_of_cap` in `infra/scripts/observability.sh:304-309` clamps: `[ "$pct" -gt 100 ] && pct=100`. The metric cannot express an overshoot. "Exactly at cap" and "over cap" are the same published number, so a cap breach renders as a healthy-looking pinned ceiling. I have filed that separately as **`undefiled-revivable-gemsbok`** (`b380-3dfc-99fc-4a0e`, p2), linked `discovered_from` this epic; it affects three metrics — `docker_storage_used_percent`, `docker_buildkit_cache_used_percent` and `journal_used_percent` — all of which are cap-compliance gauges that go blind exactly when their cap fails.

**The compounding error was mine, not just the metric's.** `rebar-docker-buildkit-cache-high` (threshold 85, GreaterThanThreshold) has been in ALARM this whole time and I discounted it as "the cap doing its job". A firing alarm was telling me the truth and I read the clamped ceiling underneath it as reassurance. That is worth recording because it is the failure mode the clamp creates: it does not merely lose precision, it converts an alarm into its opposite.

**What this does to the epic's honest position.** My earlier three-way summary needs revising:

- BuildKit budget (S0/S6): **NOT bounded in production today.** 9% over, 104 retained entries, 0 active. Whether that is a `builder.gc` configuration problem, a reclamation that is not running, or a best-effort target being treated as a hard wall is not established — `builder.gc.maxUsedSpace` is documented as best-effort, so exceeding it is not by itself proof of a defect, but it IS proof that the epic cannot claim a bound here.
- S5's reaper: bounds exited containers only, and its own report says it cannot touch a running container's writable layer. A measured **1.86 GB** currently sits in an EXITED `rebar-mcp-9d5a7278c892-8093` layer that the reaper would reclaim, so it has real work waiting for it.
- S4 `/var/tmp` and S5's per-container quota: still blocked on the `rootflags=pquota` reboot.

So of the epic's caps, one is unbounded-and-was-reported-as-bounded, one is partial by design, and two await a reboot. That is a materially weaker position than I recorded earlier tonight, and it is weaker because I mis-read the evidence, not because anything regressed in the last hour.

Root-cause diagnosis of the growth itself is on the separate comment thread; the short version is that root is a ~2 GB SAWTOOTH driven by `rebar-autodeploy.timer` rebuilding on every `main` advance with 21-minute container recreates, not the monotonic climb I originally described.
